idiom_name: protocol-conforming wrapper structs; Vapor's Middleware chain in servers
implementation_notes: A gate is a small type that conforms to the same protocol as the service it protects and holds the next service, verifying before it forwards, so gates nest as values and the protocol is the only contract - the compiler checks that every member is implemented rather than forwarded by accident. What replaces the classic structure: protocol witnesses plus value or class wrappers replace the proxy class, and in Vapor the chain is the framework's middleware list (app.middleware.use), where each middleware receives the request and either throws or returns a response, or calls next.respond(to:) - requests visit middleware in registration order and responses unwind in reverse. The classic form remains useful when the guarded type is a final class that cannot be re-wrapped or when every gate must be interposed at one generic point behind a type-erased wrapper.
pitfalls: Existential wrappers (any Service) box every call and erase specialisation, and a gate holding mutable state must be an actor or its check races under concurrency.
Vapor middleware run in registration order and responses unwind in reverse, so a gate that modifies the response after next must not write headers once the response has started.
A new protocol requirement breaks every gate unless a default implementation exists - and a default implementation that does nothing lets a gate silently skip the new check.
